definitions.explanation: The number 20,000, expressed as {二|に} (two) × {万|まん} (10,000) in the Japanese numbering system. A common round figure in everyday contexts — mid-range yen amounts, attendance figures, and so on.

examples.japanese: {入場者|にゅうじょうしゃ}は{約|やく}{二万|にまん}{人|にん}だった。
examples.english: There were about twenty thousand attendees.

examples.japanese: このコートは{二万|にまん}{円|えん}もしたのに、もう{破|やぶ}れてしまった。
examples.english: This coat cost twenty thousand yen, and it's already torn.

examples.japanese: {先月|せんげつ}、この{商品|しょうひん}は{全国|ぜんこく}で{二万|にまん}{個|こ}{以上|いじょう}{売|う}れたそうだ。
examples.english: Last month, this product reportedly sold more than twenty thousand units nationwide.

notes:
{二万|にまん} is the number 20,000. In the Japanese number system, it is formed as {二|に} (2) × {万|まん} (10,000).

JAPANESE NUMBER SYSTEM:
Japanese groups large numbers in units of 10,000 ({万|まん}), not 1,000 as in English. For twenties of thousands:
- {一万|いちまん}: 10,000
- {二万|にまん}: 20,000
- {三万|さんまん}: 30,000
- {十万|じゅうまん}: 100,000

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {二万|にまん}{円|えん}: twenty thousand yen (roughly the price of a mid-range jacket or a nice dinner for two)
- {二万|にまん}{人|にん}: twenty thousand people
- {二万|にまん}{部|ぶ}: twenty thousand copies (of a book, magazine)
- {二万|にまん}{円|えん}{札|さつ}: (colloquially) twenty-thousand-yen note — note: there is no such bill; the highest is {一万|いちまん}{円|えん}

LEARNER TIP:
{二万|にまん}{円|えん} is roughly the threshold between "moderately expensive" and "noticeably expensive" in everyday Japanese consumer contexts (a nice meal, a mid-range clothing item, a budget-level appliance).
